scope: Integration of the qualified non64 segment unit with current dev, including repair of the shared HighIR address-index regression exposed by generated continuation validators.
repair: The new DenseMap reserved InvalidVA-1/-2, which the continuation validator uses as real return labels. Restored the original unordered_map address domain; no index-clamping workaround or change to validator labels. The explicit statement-index regression checks both reserved-label collisions. The branch-only experiment did not reproduce the old crash and is retained as semantic coverage of both paths and layouts. An initial test build rejected a duplicated default argument; the redundant declaration was removed before qualification. The full control-flow suite then exposed a missing -lm in its host C compiler helper; the POSIX test harness now links the math library for scalar FMA.
boundaries: The earlier 1342-pass/2-LA57-skip primary suite per SDK remains tied to ecc5c3c22b. These integration replays are separate and are not added to its totals.

The source backends and shared IR changed upstream, so the full HighIR control-flow, paged-source, legacy-source, instruction-boundary and SDK suites were rebuilt and replayed. The lower x86 paging execution sources were unchanged upstream and their completed full baseline was not rerun.

Upstream independently advanced the LLVM source gitlink from 5676029e378c9e37adc16c8216a8e8453ffafcae to the recorded merged value. The merge preserves that history; this work did not create an LLVM release or change the production neverd-llvm-v23.0.0-r6 SDK pin.
NeverC remains host x64. The development SDK is the existing native-intrinsic compiler snapshot; the second lane uses production r6.
Code64 segment continuation, remaining full-mode owners, real/unreal/VM86 composition, software SMM/SGX, unbound event producers and physical SGX qualification are not closed by this integration.
